speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext: On the orders of the day:

speakeroldname: Hon. L. B. Pearson (Leader of the Opposiiion):
speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext:
I should like to ask the Prime Minister a question arising out of the press statement issued in the name of himself and the President of the United States yesterday evening, which is as follows:
The Canadian and United States governments have given consideration to situations where the export policies and laws of the two countries may not be in complete harmony. It has been agreed that in these cases there will be full consultation between the two governments with a view to finding through appropriate procedures satisfactory solutions to concrete problems as they arise.
I should like to ask the Prime Minister whether he can clarify the meaning of those sentences, dealing with such an important matter, in the light of the statement issued by the Minister of Finance at the same time on the same subject which reads-

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext: On a point of privilege, before my friend goes on I may say that I did not issue any press statement, so my friend should not be reading anything attributed to me under such a heading.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext:
The statement was attributed to my hon. friend by the press officer appointed by the government to hold a press conference. The press officer said that the following statement had been issued by the Minister of Finance:
The intention is that Canadian law and Canadian law alone is to prevail over persons or corporations carrying on business in Canada.

speakeroldname: Righi Hon. J. G. Diefenbaker (Prime Minister):
speakerposition: Prime Minister
maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, it would not be appropriate today to go into any detail. At the conclusion of the consultations with the President of the United States a statement will be made, and I hope that can be done tomorrow. I do not intend to be drawn into any piecemeal discussion respecting any item that may have appeared in the press or with any press report whatever. The whole question will be dealt with at one time.
Suffice it to say this: that in the discussions that have up to the moment taken place, 57071-3-132
there has been a spirit of consideration shown for each other's problems that bodes well for the future, and in particular there has been nothing in the nature, if that is what is in the mind of my hon. friend, of suggesting to the President of the United States that in regard to a matter as important as trade we should make the proposition, as suggested by the Leader of the Opposition on more than one occasion, that unless trade relations were beneficial in so far as Canada is concerned, we should threaten to withdraw or diminish in any way our defence relationships with the United States.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext: On a question of privilege, the Prime Minister has attributed remarks to me which I have never made, and which he will never be able to quote as being made by me. He should either withdraw those remarks or substantiate them.

speakerposition: Prime Minister
maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext: I have not the record here. I made a statement in the house the other day when I had the speech in question, and there was no suggestion of a denial on the part of my hon. friend at that time.

speakerposition: Speaker of the House of Commons
maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext: The Leader of the Opposition has stated in his place that he did not make such a statement. I am sure the Prime Minister will accept that statement, just as the Leader of the Opposition will accept the statement of the Minister of Finance that he did not issue a press release.

maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext: I wonder if I might ask the Prime Minister a supplementary question in this field. Will the government consider introducing in this house legislation that would require Canadian subsidiaries of United States companies to act in the export field in such a way as to bring advantage to Canada and not in accordance with the laws in some other country?

speakerposition: Prime Minister
maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext:
I do not think any
legislation to that effect would be helpful in any way. I am not going into the complexities of the situation that would be created as the result of legislation to that effect, but when the report is made tomorrow I am sure the hon. gentleman will agree that Canada's subsidiaries will not in any way be interfered with in so far as entering into contracts with other countries

Trade
is concerned in respect of those things which Canada does not consider strategic.

maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext:
In view of the importance of this matter, may I ask the Minister of Finance whether these words used by the press officer on behalf of the government of Canada represent the situation in so far as it is within the minister's knowledge? Mr. Nelson said:
I have an explanatory note here that might help, given to me by the Minister of Finance: The intention is that Canadian law and Canadian law alone is to prevail over persons or corporations carrying on business in Canada.
Q. That's the same thing as consultation?

maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext:
That's what they hope to achieve by it.
In view of the importance of this matter to my constituency and many others, will the Minister of Finance not clarify this matter at once?

speakeroldname: Hon. Donald M. Fleming (Minister of Finance):
speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, my hon. friend knows perfectly well that the only law that is binding upon Canadians when in Canada or corporations that are doing business in Canada, to the extent to which they are doing business in Canada lawfully, is the law of Canada.

maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext: That is right.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext: The question that arises here concerns the relations of Canadian subsidiaries to their parent corporations in the United States. My hon. friend knows well that that is a complex matter. I think he has heard the very proper suggestion by the Prime Minister that the matter should not be dealt with piecemeal, that a complicated question of that kind cannot be dealt with in justice in any piecemeal manner. I think my hon. friend would be the first to say that this matter should be dealt with in the manner proposed by the Prime Minister following the conclusion of his meetings with the President of the United States.

maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext: Will the Minister of Finance not agree with me that the Prime Minister's observations a few moments ago really represent what should be the situation from now on? But does the Minister of Finance not think that the statement which he authorized the press officer to make has complicated the situation, and is certainly not consistent with the statement he has just made in answer to my question?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, I am always happy to find myself in disagreement with my hon. friend.

speakerposition: Prime Minister
maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, arising out of the question of privilege raised by the Leader of the Opposition, I would refer him to the comments he made on May 13, 1958 as recorded at page 25 of Hansard, which read as follows:
We must naturally protect our interests when they are prejudiced by United States policy. We must, for instance, make It quite clear that the United States cannot expect full and complete co-operation in continental defence, which is desirable, if she treats us unfairly in her tariff and trade policies.

maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext: Hear, hear.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
maintopic: REQUEST FOR CLARIFICATION OF JOINT PRESS STATEMENT
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, the Prime Minister has done what he said last night to the press, in connection with the speech of the President of the United States, he would never do. He said he would never take a sentence out of context and draw a conclusion from it. But apart from that, even taking the meaning which he gave to this sentence-and he should have gone on to quote my further remarks on this same page of Hansard-it does not conform to what he said a few moments ago.
Furthermore, I would like to ask the Prime Minister whether he disagrees with the particular sentence he has quoted.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext: On the orders of the day:

speakerposition: Minister of Labour
subtopic: STATEMENT ON REPORTED CRITICISM OF ACT BY MONTREAL JUDGE
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, the hon. member for Vancouver East yesterday referred to a situation with respect to unemployment insurance in the city of Montreal in respect to which, as he put it, there had occurred strong criticism on the part of a judge regarding the provisions of the Unemployment Insurance Act which deprive a person of benefits if he obtains any casual employment.
I should inform the hon. member, Mr. Speaker, that there are no such provisions. A certain supplementary income is permitted and benefits are graded accordingly. For example, in the case of a person drawing $30 weekly he is permitted to earn up to $13, granting him a total of $43. A person drawing $21 is permitted to earn up to $8, giving him a total of $29. Benefits are not withdrawn; they are graded down according to the amount a person earns. The recipient must, of course, report these casual earnings.
I should inform the hon. member that the gentleman in question was taken to court not under the Unemployment Insurance Act but under a provision in the Criminal Code against misrepresentation. The charge was based on the fact that he had earned money which he had failed to declare while at the same time collecting unemployment insurance. Covering a period of three different weeks he had declared $12, while actual earnings were computed at $93. In addition he had collected $90 in unemployment insurance. In all he had collected $56 more than his entitlement.
As regards the third question, amendments to the act are now being considered and I hope they can be brought down this session.
